chok-yaakov/2:_: As long as there are no shepherds to eat from it. It means that restraining a lot of people who even consider it to eat in their minds:
beur-hagra/1:א: 1. One does not fulfill. As explained ch. 2 Challah: mursan removed etc.; same for matzah — one law, as ch. 20 and Menachot 41b:
beur-hagra/1:ב: But kneading etc. There they are: se'or, sovin, mursan — five quarters etc.; ch. Kol Sha'ah 37a in hadra'ah — see Rosh there:
beur-hagra/1:ג: And good etc. There 36b — see Rashi there s.v. ashisha; so in gemara ashisha one etc.:
beur-hagra/1:ד: That it is not. As written there 38b:
beur-hagra/2:_: Seif 2 but some say the reason. As in Challah there exempt from challah — must be because of bread; so all matters there listed are because of bread; Rambam also holds so, only added here even fit for shepherds who eat — since made only for dogs exempt, not meshumar as above:
beur-hagra/3:א: Seif 3 there is none. So Rif, Rosh, Rambam; so Geonim forbade it; all in it because they press flour or put in sack and chalut and dikula of water from four winds does not ascend — as written 40a not to chalut etc.; Rambam wrote reason deceased will not boil water properly:
beur-hagra/3:ב: Therefore all types. Meaning types of chalita from which one does not fulfill b'dieved; as Tosafot there 36b s.v. prat and Yevamot 40a: thick kneading like soft, made in sun, thick kneading even baked in oven — for Rav like chalut in oil:
beur-hagra/4:א: Seif 4 no person. From what is written 38a "what is yours" etc. — see Rosh there:
beur-hagra/4:ב: When is this said. In Yerushalmi brought by Rosh: one might think at first etc.; Rosh explained l'chatchila; b'dieved fulfills — but ruled like latter amoraim there who hold even b'dieved not; nevertheless ch. 6 he explained as Shulchan Aruch here — stolen matzah etc.:
beur-hagra/4:ג: But if stole. Yerushalmi ch. 3 Sukkah: stole shovel — but if lent and planed, payment owed; as Tosafot Sukkah 30a: even after ye'ush acquisition — nevertheless forbidden mitzvah haba'ah ba'aveirah specifically acquired through transgression with ye'ush in order we hold Bava Kamma ch. Merubah and ch. Hagozel batra not acquired except through shinui reshus — in hadas and lulav because shinui reshus through mitzvah; therefore challenges in Merubah for one who holds ye'ush with intent acquires — sacrifice not stolen; why not after ye'ush? Because not mitzvah haba'ah ba'aveirah since already acquired through ye'ush per his view:
beur-hagra/4:ד: And regarding blessing. As Bava Kamma 94a: stole se'ah etc.; Rava there mitzvah haba'ah ba'aveirah; Tosafot Sukkah there for blessing although already acquired; and although Yerushalmi Rosh brought — comes like Abaye in Bava Kamma there:
chok-yaakov/1:א: In bread of sovin not bread of mursan. Sovin and mursan are same — sovin is thick hull of grain, mursan thin; Rashi Shabbat ch. 7 and Ra'avad ch. 2 Challah; Peirushim on Terumot opposite; Magen Avraham: somewhat proves causes chimutz since fulfill per Rif; possible since species that causes chimutz — fulfills obligation; saw mursan called shafiryar does not chametz — but hard hull; wheat hull itself perhaps causes chimutz; impossible no wheat substance adheres — end Magen Avraham (see Peirushim Terumot mishnah 5: new wheat sovin much flour mixed, not old — Ra'avad). I wonder at his uncertainty — why doubt? Complete mishnah: do not soak mursan for chickens — causes chimutz siman 465; how hidden from him? If oat spike found in dissolved food without grain — perhaps wheat fell in — see Torat HaShelamim; all fell at harvest time we do not establish prohibition; rabbinic something — Machatzit HaShekel s.k. 5; if three spikes need examination:
chok-yaakov/1:ב: In sovin and mursan in it. If separated mursan and returned and kneaded — Magen Avraham uncertain if joins kezayit; see YD 324; in my humble opinion no doubt — since for challah does not join, same for matzah as Beit Yosef — interdependent; so Mishnah Berurah; Rashba in Peskei Challah agrees; language of poskim "in sovin and mursan in it" specifically; Ran: same if wheat worms ate:
chok-yaakov/4:א: Stolen matzah. Clear in Yerushalmi: specifically stolen matzah invalid because matzah itself in transgression; not so carrying matzah private to public — fulfills on Pesach — transgression of carrying not matzah in transgression; so Torat Adam Rashba 21b; Tosafot Sukkah 30 s.v. because of division; Taz: fulfills borrowed matzah since not returned in kind; Acharonim and Rokeach: good to say at grinding or baking gift formula:
chok-yaakov/4:ב: Regarding blessing see siman 649. Intent on ruling there: although acquired through ye'ush and shinui — still no blessing — "cuts blesses, curses"; no difference shinui shem or shinui ma'aseh; as Bava Kamma end regarding challah: stole se'ah wheat, ground, baked, separated challah — blesses not curses though shinui ma'aseh and shem; most poskim; Tosafot Sukkah 30, Merubah 69, Nezikin 55, Rosh ch. Hagozel; Bach and Acharonim above 196; not Magen Avraham 649 s.k. 2 distinguishing shem and ma'aseh — not so. On Magen Avraham's question from Sukkah 30 regarding onkari (Rashi: merchants) — gemara challenges acquisition through shinui shem and ma'aseh forbidden bless — not difficult: forbidden bless is full theft as stole se'ah — not there remote concern of mitzvah stringency; know Rav Huna commanded only hoshana mitzvah not all things taken to detach; gemara challenges onkari themselves — Rav Huna commanded how do l'chatchila teach theft? Certainly no theft — only mitzvah stringency (see Shach CM 319, Yam Shel Shlomo Bava Kamma, Sha'ar Efraim siman 2 theft prohibition). Taz erred later 464 s.k. 16 thinking full theft — challenges Hagozel batra and Rava — did not notice contradiction proving not theft only mitzvah concern. On Taz's question why poskim omitted Rav Huna — strained answer; poskim' main reason from Gittin ch. 5: minors no anporot in Bavel — poskim: since judges and kingdom law and did not claim illness exemption — no theft; permitted take though no ye'ush in land as Rambam ch. 10 Gezeilah, Tur CM 256 — Beit Yosef; resolves Shpati Kohen Choshen Mishpat 107, 471; Rambam required, not Tosafot ch. Chezkat Batim; expanded in my Choshen Mishpat; see Shpati Kohen 195 standing to detach as detached:
peri-megadim/1:_: Not Taz — even fit for eating like new grain fit for eating — Magen Avraham 1; or took sovin and mursan and returned — flour fit for human food — nevertheless if challah: without five quarters flour aside from sovin not obligated challah; if took sovin and returned — Magen Avraham 2: "bread" written — not bread for most; or "your doughs" — also derive matzah gezeirah shavah lechem from there "for you"; nevertheless if took sovin returned and kezayit flour — fulfills, for all agree for us Torah dough 463 — Magen Avraham 4; opening and Challah ch. 2 mishnah 6: took sovin returned exempt when no challah measure except flour — Bach: if kezayit flour fulfills as said; Peri Chadash:
peri-megadim/2:_: For Taz Pesachim 36b lechem oni excludes chalut and ashisha — implies impediment; gemara ashisha one of six per ephah — Peri Chadash; uncertain why poskim did not mention explicitly:
peri-megadim/3:_: That it is not Taz — Mechaber ruled like Rambam even fit for human food, clean flour — all made for beast and guarded from leavening — still invalid, not guarded for matzah mitzvah; as Pesachim 38b challah of thanksgiving etc.; Rav Huna Pesachim 40a gentile doughs etc. if eats kezayit matzah at end — same here; Mishna Berurah as Tur YD 330: when shepherds do not eat — not fit, much sovin — invalid; if fit for eating — fulfills; challah of thanksgiving worse — guarded for sacrifice not matzah mitzvah; gentile doughs l'chatchila, b'dieved even not guarded from kneading onward — all not leavened fulfills; Mishna Berurah did not correct Tosafot three six — perhaps relied here; it appears ch. 8, 9 double. Apparently ch. 8: reason "your doughs" not for beast as Ra'avad ch. 1 mishnah 8; ch. 9: even for shepherds if not fit — exempt; if so what is "specifically recognizable for dogs"? Both deal with fit for man as Beer HaGolah. From "your doughs" difficult to exclude gentile like beast — Yom Tov; but "in your food from land" different; Yerushalmi Challah dispute R' Yochanan, R' Yehoshua, Rava — if R' Yochanan made like blocks liable (Nissan recognizable for beast) exempt — we require changed bread form; in bread form even for beast liable; gentile in bread form liable. Abaye asked why exempt clean bank — wrote from "your doughs" or "in your food"; Mishna Berurah corrected Tur/Rosh: specifically shepherds unfit — if fit fulfills even for dogs — bread form obligated challah; Mechaber invalid not meshumar — Magen Avraham sign 3 explained there; Beit Yosef YD 330 Rambam exempt even challah in bread form — like Rava, disagrees R' Yehoshua; Levush: eaten under duress not meshumar; not human food — uncertain Mechaber view even clean flour invalid; Peri Megadim sign 3. Practically if ate matzah made for man eaten only under duress — Peri Megadim 14 from Magen Avraham 11: not normal eating exempt; same mitzvah; Magen Avraham Levush 246. Mishnah there: in any case impure 9 — must be fit for man under duress; or already received impurity — Ra'avad, Rambam, Tosefta. Unleavened on Yom Tov — even clean flour only for dogs — Rambam laws Yom Tov:
peri-megadim/4:א: In matzah Taz — Peri Chadash 4, Kaf HaChayyim sign 5: one who carries matzah private to public and eats — fulfills as Yerushalmi — not mitzvah haba'ah ba'aveirah, for without transgression too could fulfill positive command — see there. If permitted for carrier to eat — Chayei Adam 318, 307. There 318: positive command Israel rabbinic prohibition — Levush for evening preparation; Avot Rabbi Natan sign 4; written from this. Perhaps carrying public to private — uncertain. Implies if baked Shabbat and ate — Magen Avraham invalid as cooking; perhaps could bake erev:
peri-megadim/4:ב: One who ate matzah of rabbinic prohibition — invalid as challah outside land etc. — Pesachim 35b; Rashi there even only tevel matzah invalid; for us rabbinic prohibition included — fulfills only if no other matzah; if other matzah — invalid as cooking; Tosafot Kiddushin 38a s.v. dakrav — positive does not override negative before Sinai or rabbinic first kezayit — see there; rabbinic prohibition perhaps double decree; Tosefta 1: all Torah prohibition does not override — same rabbinic established — Magen Avraham 246:2, Rambam ch. 6 positive commandment 10: all not bless hamazon invalid — even rabbinic prohibition if has other matzah — cooking. Perhaps wine four cups or maror rabbinic — positive rabbinic overrides rabbinic negative — Magen Avraham 487:2; at time called; can eat kezayit and revi'it Bava Kamma — Yerushalmi, 475 explained further. Chayei Adam 119: suspected host Pesach — no other matzah — uncertain; explained 475, 485:
